To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have developed and evaluated two novel approaches for motion artifacts removal from electrocardiographic signals, (2) the first approach is based on the use of an accelerometer to measure electrode motion and to use this measurement to design adaptive filters to remove motion noise, (3) the second approach is based in the use of independent component analysis methods to separate the different sources of the ECG signal.
the proposed approaches can be used to reduce the motion artifacts in ECG signal, thus allowing a better analysis of the signal.

1) the use of an accelerometer to measure electrode motion allows to reduce motion artifacts in the ECG; 2) the instantaneous model of ICA can be successfully applied to multichannels ECG recordings to get rid of the confounding motion artifacts; 3) a frequency domain implementation can also provide good performances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the removal of artifacts from multichannel ECOG recordings.
the design of algorithms that are able to detect, characterize and remove motion artifacts from multichannel electrocardiographic signals.
the development of a new method for the removal of motion artifacts from ECG signals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of multichannel EOG signals is a promising approach for the development of an automatic system that could be used to monitor and detect sleep disorders.
the proposed methods are able to effectively remove motion confounds from ECG signals, and that the best performances are obtained with the multichannel approaches.
the use of the multichannel approach in combination with the use of accelerometers is the most promising approach for removing motion artifacts.

we propose two different methods for removing motion artifacts from ECG signals.
the first approach is more effective for removing the noise in the ECG, while the second one is more robust to different types of artifacts and it can be applied to any multichannel EKG signal.
the proposed methods have been tested on simulated data and on real recordings.

multichannel ECK acquisition and processing is the key to remove motion artifacts.
